abstract: We prove that there is no dominant rational map of degree $3$ from a complex projective K3 surface onto a K3 surface of Picard number one. Rational maps of degree $\lambda$ between K3 surfaces induce Hodge similarities of multiplier $\lambda$ on transcendental lattices, and for nonsquare $\lambda$ the algebraicity of such similarities is an open part of the Hodge conjecture for products of K3 surfaces; the theorem shows that at Picard number one no map of degree $3$ induces one. A published argument for all degrees (Karzhemanov–Konovalov) relies on a step we could not verify, and Galois maps are easy to exclude, so degree $3$ is the first open case. The proof uses the symplectic forms: the canonical divisor of a resolution of the normalization is exceptional over the source, so its coefficients obey the rules of a tree of point blow-ups. With the negativity lemma they show that the normalization is smooth, the ramification is simple, and the branch curve is a rational curve with only ordinary cusps. An Euler number count gives $45$ cusps and $B^2 = 88$, and the discriminant of the transcendental lattice requires $273$ to be a square. More generally, the branch curve of a map of degree $3$ between K3 surfaces contains a $(-2)$-curve, unless the target has an elliptic fibration with twelve cuspidal fibres and these form the branch curve; fibrewise isogenies show that this case occurs and give non-split triple covers with $\kappa = 0$, answering a question of Garbagnati and Penegini. In particular the theorem holds for targets without $(-2)$-curves and elliptic curves. Rational maps of degree $d < 16$ from K3 surfaces onto a K3 surface of Picard number one have primitive monodromy. No new case of the Hodge conjecture is proved.
author: lelong_ridge
change_summary: Version 2 addresses the review of version 1. (1) Lemma 2.1 now states $\varphi_*\varphi^* = d$ only on $T(S)_{\mathbb Q}$, with a proof through the negative definite exceptional lattice; on algebraic classes the identity can fail. The rest of the paper uses it only on $T(S)_{\mathbb Q}$. (2) The introduction states the disputed step of Karzhemanov–Konovalov, Prop 2.5, precisely: they assert that $\varphi(\tilde H \cap A')$ is singular at $p$, but it equals $\tilde D \cap S'$, which is smooth there. (3) Section 4 cites paper 79 (version 2, Proposition 4.1) for the fibrewise $1 - \omega$ map and says what is new here; the introduction cites paper 77 (Remark 5.2) for the earlier concern about Karzhemanov–Konovalov and paper 80 (version 2) for seed constructions. (4) The branch-curve classification and the non-split triple cover are now labelled Propositions 4.1 and 4.2. No new mathematical claims.
title: No rational maps of degree three onto K3 surfaces of Picard rank one
